 Weather Alert
 ...FLOOD WATCH IN EFFECT FROM SATURDAY EVENING THROUGH EARLY MONDAY
MORNING...
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.
* WHERE...A portion of Southeast Arizona, including the following
areas, Baboquivari Mountains, Catalina and Rincon Mountains,
Dragoon and Mule and Huachuca and Santa Rita Mountains, Galiuro and
Pinaleno Mountains, South Central Pinal County, Southeast Pinal
County, Tohono O'odham Nation, Tucson Metro Area, Upper Gila River
Valley, Upper San Pedro River Valley, Upper Santa Cruz River
Valley/Altar Valley and White Mountains of Graham and Greenlee
Counties.
* WHEN...From Saturday evening through early Monday morning.
* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.
* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A strong weather system approaching the area will bring
widespread to numerous showers Sunday, November 1. Moderate to
locally heavy rainfall with rainfall totals 0.5 to 1 inch
possible in the valleys and 1 to 2+ inches possible in the
mountains.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

 If you are 65 and older, open enrollment for Medicare coverage is officially underway. However, the 2027 plan year brings several significant changes that enrollees need to prepare for. While the original federal Medicare plans (Parts A, B, and D) remain standard, a major shift is happening with Part C, commonly known as Medicare Advantage. Several private insurance companies are dropping their Medicare Advantage plans for 2027, which means some seniors will need to find new coverage if their current provider no longer offers their plan next year. In addition to dropped coverage, seniors can expect higher expenses across all plans. Medicare Part B premiums are on the rise, deductibles are increasing, and the cap for out-of-pocket costs on prescription drugs is going up.
